Consult Summary:
- 27-year-old male with 3 days of profuse watery diarrhea (nearly hourly when awake), intermittent lower midline crampy abdominal pain (~6/10), nausea with occasional vomiting (notably after milk), and subjective fevers without measured temperature.
- No blood in stool. Passing urine less frequently but still passing. Brother had similar illness for ~5 days. Clinical impression: acute gastroenteritis. Managed conservatively with hydration, oral rehydration salts, soft diet, paracetamol; advised to avoid alcohol and to call back in 48 hours if not improving.

Problem List:

Issue 1:
- Acute gastroenteritis with dehydration risk
  - Onset/duration: ~3 days.
  - Symptoms: Profuse watery diarrhea nearly hourly when awake; intermittent crampy lower abdominal pain (midline), comes and goes, patient-estimated ~6/10; nausea; episodic vomiting (worse after milk); feeling “hot”/subjective fever without temperature taken; decreased urination frequency.
  - Pertinent negatives: No visible blood in stool.
  - Context: Brother with similar symptoms for ~5 days (possible infectious contact). No clear dietary trigger identified.
  - Functional impact: Attending work is difficult.
  - Clinical impression: Gastroenteritis (doctor’s assessment).
  - Plan: Oral rehydration salts (Diarolyte/Dioralyte—name varied in transcript) OTC, clear fluids, soft diet (soup, mashed foods), advance as tolerated; paracetamol for fever/pain; avoid alcohol; reassess if not improving in 48 hours; consider further investigation if dehydration develops.

Issue 2:
- Family history of colon cancer
  - Father currently has colon cancer; patient believes “third stage” but uncertain of details.

Issue 3:
- Tobacco and alcohol use
  - Tobacco: Social smoker (occasional, e.g., on Fridays).
  - Alcohol: Occasional beer on weekdays; heavier intake on Fridays; binge drinking once or twice per month. Advised to avoid alcohol during current illness.

Medications:
- Paracetamol (dose/route/frequency not documented).

Allergies:
- No known drug allergies.

Past Medical History:
- No chronic medical conditions reported; otherwise fit and well.

Social History:
- Lives with mother and sister; brother does not live with patient.
- Works in a government office in Central London.
- Smoking: Social/occasional.
- Alcohol: Occasional; binge episodes 1–2 times/month.

Preventative History:
- Not discussed.

Physical Examination:
- No vitals recorded.
- No physical examination performed (audio-only telehealth consult).

Plan:
- Hydration: Use oral rehydration salts (ORS) such as Diarolyte/Dioralyte (OTC); maintain clear fluids.
- Diet: Soft diet (soup, mashed foods); gradually advance as tolerated.
- Symptom control: Continue paracetamol for fever/pain.
- Lifestyle: Avoid alcohol during illness.
- Follow-up/safety net: If symptoms are not improving within 48 hours, call back. If dehydration worsens, further investigations will be needed.

Quality checks:
- Missing expected elements: No vitals, no physical exam, no objective temperature, no stool frequency log beyond “hourly,” no travel/antibiotic exposure history, no recent food exposure details, no medication dosing, no vaccination/preventive care history.
- Internal conflicts: ORS brand name varied (Diarolyte vs Dioralyte). Doctor briefly stated “you’re feeling hoarse” without supporting patient report (likely transcript artifact).
- Transcript quality: Occasional audio interruptions/overlap; some unclear segments; overall adequate to determine key clinical details.
